title: Ice-age crustal rebound as the cause of pole shift
place_text: North America, Hudson Bay, northwestern Europe

tellings.quote: I think that what happens is is that with the process of glaciation, rapid glaciation or rapid deglaciation, it induces a tremendous amount of instability in the Earth's crust that could manifest as an accelerated episode of continental of of lithospheric movement.

plain: When ice sheets grow or melt quickly, as in the Ice Age over North America, Hudson Bay and northwestern Europe, they may shake up the Earth's crust so much that its outer shell slides faster, shifting where the poles sit. The researcher Randall Carlson tells Michels this as his own view, building on the earlier writer Charles Hapgood and on a lecture of his own about Atlantis. If true, it would mean sudden changes to the Earth's surface in humanity's past.
